newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Week starts slowly.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Week starts slowly.

text.p: Asian debt markets started the week off slowly, but there are a number of transactions scheduled for launch later this week.
Philippine conglomerate Ayala Corp is expected to launch a US$75 million floating rate note issue through its special purpose vehicle AC International Finance on Wednesday.
Bankers Trust Asia is the arranger.

The issue has a final maturity of five years and there are no put or call options. It is expected to pay a coupon of 90 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate and an all-in return of about 100 basis points.
Bankers Trust also is tipped to lead a US$75 million FRN for PT Surya Dumai Industri Finance Co.

Many other Indonesian deals are waiting in the wings, including FRNs for many of the state and private banks. A number of Indonesian corporates also are lining up for new loan and capital markets issues.
Korean bank deals also are on the outlook.

Hana Bank's US$100 million FRN is scheduled for launch on Thursday. That deal has a five-year final maturity and puts and calls in year three. The all-in return is expected to be around 36.5 basis points over LIBOR.
Arrangers are Citicorp International, DKB Asia, Dresdner SEA, IBJ Asia and Banca Nationale del Lavoro.
Cho Hung Bank has mandated Citicorp International and Fuji International Finance to arrange a US$200 million floating rate note issue, bankers said Monday.
The facility has a final maturity of three years with no put or call options. It is expected to be priced at par to float at 20 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
General syndication is expected to begin within the next several days.
On the loan side, Thailand's Tanayong said it would borrow US$80 million through a transferable loan certificate facility to partially finance its Bangkok rail mass transit system.

In other debt news, South Korean bond traders said Monday that South Korea's bid to boost private-sector investment in infrastructure projects by allowing developers to issue long maturity bonds could spur the growth of a long-term debt market.
